questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city of Boston, academic opportunities, and experiencing the "college" life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Boston University (BU) is very proactive and willing to help. We had an exchange coordinator who we could always contact if in doubt. Also, she emailed us all the relevant information before arriving.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot. We met with our exchange coordinator during the first week, had a guide to show us around campus, and lots more.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You have to prioritize a list of a few options, but in reality BU places you were there is open spots. Right new the biggest dorm is being renovated (Warren Towers), so most exchange students (around 220 people) were placed in a hotel nearby (Hyatt Regency in Cambridge). A few also lived in Warren Towers (there are 3 towers, so some students are still living there) and some in West campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
Almost everyone I know bought the full dining plan. It is very expensive, but also very nice. It works as a meeting spot, and helps you focus on school and your social life. 

For those who stayed at the Hotel, it was mandatory to buy the plan as we do not have the possible to cook. This also goes for those staying in dorms. Only if you live off campus or in apartments through BU can you cook for yourself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
On campus is the most common for new students at BU. Some master students and a few exchange students also chose to stay off campus. 

I recommend living on campus as you meet a lot of new people this way. Also, it is very neat to stay close to campus, and living off campus is very expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you know someone from KU or another university who is also going to BU, you can request to live together. I did this with a friend from KU, and we had a great time living together in the hotel room.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a portal for this. It is very easy to browse available courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the opening day for registration. Full-time BU students get to choose before exchange students, so it is important to be ready when they open for registration. 
With that said, I also change a course after getting here, and attended a few that I did not like. Most people end up getting all the courses that they want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
The portal. Also, you chan reach out to the exchange coordinator. 

I also contacted a few professors directly and asked for a spot in the class. I successfully got spots on both. These were graduate courses, and usually they don't allow for undergraduate students to participate in graduate courses, but I got lucky. If you show prerequisites and interest in the class, they will maybe allow you to join.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach out to professor - they are very helpfull and want you in class if you show interest. They like exchange students as we are typically very dedicated and mature.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level varied a bit from class to class. For me, the level was similar to KU, but I also had two graduate classes instead of choosing only undergraduate. Most find the level a bit lower compared to KU, but it really does depend a lot on the classes you take. 

The classes are ranked in levels (1 through 8). So all classes being between 100-199 are level 1 and so on. 100-400 is undergraduate, and above 500 is graduate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is actually quite different. 

We are use to big lecture with around 200-300 people and exercise classes at KU. At BU, most classes are around 10-40 people. It is almost a high-school teaching style, and you typically feel closer to your professor. It is also more common to ask questions in class, and most professors also care about participation. In some classes, a percentage of your grade is based on participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- EC365 B1 Economic Institutions in Historical Perspective (transferred as: Økonomisk Historie)
- EC403 A1 Game Theory (transferred as: microeconomics III)
- EC502 Macroeconomic Theory (transferred as: macroeconomics III)
- EC545 Financial Economics (transferred as: prioritised elective) This class is similar to Financial Decision Making at KU.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend all of them. I got very lucky with getting my classes transferred to some KU classes that I would have to take back home anyway. 

If you are into business, I recommend considering some classes at Questroom - school of business. I were supposed to have a class there (Investment Banking), but decided to drop it as I found the others more interesting.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: You get $280 worth of "dining points" from your dining plan. Those can be spent at places like Panda Express, Raising Canes, Dominos etc. They can also be spend on coffee or snacks from the convenience store.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Boston is a sports city! 
We have the Celtics, Bruins, BU's hockey teams (they are ranked 5. in the entire country right now), Patriots, Red Sox and if you dare: Boston College Football. Boston College is close by, and we were lucky to get some danish and norwegian friends from BC, so we went to the games together. BC and BU kind of have a rivalry, but it is a lot of fun to watch their football games, as BU does not have a football team.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Endless activities. There are so many clubs. You have the possibility to join all of them. I tried out for the basketball club team, and I had friends playing volleyball, tennis, dancing etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not attend many, so I am not the one to ask.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on extended weekend trips!
I went to:
- New York
- White Mountains
- Kennebunkport
- Newport
- Miami

NY is a must in my opinion. Miami was good fun because we went as a big group, but this is more of a party city. The rest on my list are more relaxed and very "New England"-style.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Very easy. People are so welcoming. My main friend group was 8 Danes, but we hung out with Italians, Spanish, Japanese, Irish, British, and of course locals. 

Boston all in all is a very European city, so there was no big culture chok.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Be ready during orientation week! People are very open to new friendships. 

Try to find other exchange or transfer students (BU will definitely help you with this. They put all of us in the same orientation group, so we naturally fond each other on the first day.)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that many. But naturally you speak English a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The New England lifestyle is very nice. People are nice here.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You won't regret it. It is a lot of money, but it is so much worth it. You get friendships and experiences for life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friendships I can bring back to Copenhagen (danish friends), academic opportunities, and I feel like I found my academic focus for my bachelor thesis and masters here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends, family, and girlfriend for 4 months. Maybe also the time difference can be a bit annoying when wanting to connect with connections in DK.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
